title: Skin
description: Facial and perioral skin conditions a GDP might encounter or be the first to notice.

title: Lips
description: Conditions affecting the vermilion, the angles of the mouth, and the perioral skin.

title: Cheeks
description: Conditions affecting the buccal mucosa, from benign keratotic variants to inflammatory and potentially malignant lesions.

title: Tongue
description: Conditions affecting the dorsal surface, lateral borders, and ventral surface of the tongue — inflammatory, infective, pigmentary, haematological, and malignant.

title: Floor of mouth
description: Lesions arising in the floor of the mouth — including cystic swellings from the sublingual gland, obstructive salivary gland disease, life-threatening deep-space infections, and the single highest-risk site for oral squamous cell carcinoma.

title: Palate
description: Conditions affecting the hard and soft palate — the roof of the mouth — including candidal infections under dentures, bony outgrowths, smoking-related keratosis, dental abscesses pointing palatally, and salivary gland swellings.

title: Throat
description: Oropharyngeal conditions a GDP might encounter or need to refer — from sore throat in the waiting room to an HPV-driven cancer hiding behind a tonsil.

title: Muscles
description: Conditions affecting the masticatory and orofacial muscles — pain, restricted opening, and muscle-driven deformity.

title: Periodontal
description: Diseases of the gum and the supporting structures of the teeth — gingiva, PDL, cementum, alveolar bone.

title: Primary dentition
description: Conditions of the primary teeth in children — from early decay patterns through pulp disease, infection, trauma, and eruption disturbances.

title: Permanent dentition
description: Diseases and complications of the adult dentition — caries, pulp and periapical pathology, tooth wear, trauma, and developmental defects.

title: Fixed prosthesis
description: Failure and complication modes of crowns, bridges, veneers, post-core restorations, and implant-supported crowns.

title: Removable prosthesis
description: Problems caused by or related to complete and partial dentures — tissue injury, retention loss, occlusal errors, and structural failure.

title: Psychological
description: Psychological and behavioural conditions that present with oral signs or that shape how patients engage with dental care.

title: Lifestyle
description: Oral conditions where the primary driver is a lifestyle factor: tobacco use, dietary acid or sugar patterns, and oral hygiene habits.

title: Jaw
description: Pathology of the maxilla and mandible — odontogenic and non-odontogenic cysts, jaw tumours, fibro-osseous diseases, deep-space infections, maxillary sinus problems, and dento-alveolar / facial-skeleton fractures.

title: Salivary glands
description: Diseases of the major (parotid, submandibular, sublingual) and minor salivary glands — obstructive, infective, inflammatory, autoimmune, and neoplastic.

title: Craniofacial syndromes
description: Congenital and developmental syndromes affecting the face, jaws, palate, and dentition — most are referred to specialist multidisciplinary care, but the GDP is often first to notice.

title: Neurogenic pain
description: Facial and oral pain of neurogenic, vascular, or central origin — the differentials for the toothache that doesn't behave like a toothache.

title: Systemic disease
description: Oral and dental manifestations of systemic disease — the moment when a routine dental exam picks up an undiagnosed haematological, endocrine, autoimmune, or metabolic condition.
